title: Multiplayer Laptop Design Comparison
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D laptop design comparison scene using Three.js. The scene simulates a multiplayer product review where two virtual 'reviewers' each have a laptop pedestal, and users can switch between designs and compare ratings.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Create a ground plane (20x20, color #2a2a2a) at y=0.
- Create two pedestals (BoxGeometry 1.5x0.5x1.5, color #444444) positioned at (-2.5, 0.25, 0) and (2.5, 0.25, 0). These represent Pedestal A (left) and Pedestal B (right).
- On each pedestal, place a laptop representation: a flat box (1.2x0.05x0.8, color #111111) as the base at y=0.525 on each pedestal, and a thinner box (1.2x0.8x0.02) as the screen, rotated -70 degrees on X axis, positioned appropriately above the base hinge.
- Load the 'Avocado.glb' model using GLTFLoader (from CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale it to 8x and place it at (0, 0.5, -3) as a decorative mascot/branding element on the comparison table.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.

LAPTOP DESIGNS:
- Define 3 design variants: 'Slim' (screen color #1a1aff), 'Pro' (screen color #ff4444), 'Ultra' (screen color #00cc66).
- Pedestal A starts with design index 0 ('Slim'), Pedestal B starts with design index 1 ('Pro').
- The screen box material color changes to reflect the current design.

UI ELEMENTS:
- Add a title div at top center: 'Laptop Design Comparison' in white, 24px font.
- Add two buttons: 'Cycle Design A' (id='btnCycleA') and 'Cycle Design B' (id='btnCycleB') positioned at bottom-left and bottom-right respectively.
- Add a 'Compare' button (id='btnCompare') at bottom center that triggers a comparison.
- Add a status div (id='statusText') below the title showing current designs: 'A: Slim | B: Pro'.
- Add a comparison result div (id='compareResult') that is initially empty.

INTERACTIONS:
- Clicking 'Cycle Design A' cycles Pedestal A's laptop through designs: Slim->Pro->Ultra->Slim...
- Clicking 'Cycle Design B' cycles Pedestal B's laptop through designs similarly.
- Clicking 'Compare' sets the compareResult text. If both are the same design, show 'Same design selected!'. Otherwise show 'Comparing: [DesignA] vs [DesignB]'.
- Pressing keyboard key 'R' resets both pedestals to initial state (A=Slim, B=Pro) and clears comparison result.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - designIndexA: number (0=Slim, 1=Pro, 2=Ultra)
  - designIndexB: number
  - designNameA: string
  - designNameB: string
  - comparisonDone: boolean (true after Compare clicked)
  - comparisonResult: string (the comparison text)
  - avocadoLoaded: boolean (true once Avocado.glb loads)
  - pedestalCount: 2
  - resetCount: number (increments each time R is pressed)
  - sceneReady: boolean (true after full init)

Make sure all state updates happen synchronously with user actions. The scene should be fully functional in a single HTML file with all dependencies loaded from CDN.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Laptop screen colors must update immediately on design cycle. State values must always be consistent (designIndexA must match designNameA, etc.).
